title: Function Machine
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Functions drawn as machines: argument tokens enter chutes named after the parameters and the return value comes out, including a write-your-own lambda.

learningObjectives: Explain a function as a machine that turns arguments into a return value
Match each argument to the parameter name it is assigned to
Create a one-line lambda function and test it with different arguments

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Concrete metaphor with input-output experimentation and creation
keyQuestions: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
How can one function return three values?
When is a lambda a better choice than def?
commonMisconceptions: print() inside a function is the same as return
Parameters keep their values after the function ends
A lambda can hold several statements
assessmentOpportunities: Students predict `to_12_hour(0)` and `to_12_hour(12)` before running them.
Students write a working two-parameter lambda.
Students explain the difference between a parameter and an argument using the chute picture.

controls.label: Function
controls.description: Chooses to_12_hour, split_seconds, add or Write your own

controls.label: Run
controls.description: Calls the function and animates the tokens

controls.label: Lambda
controls.description: A one-line lambda for Write your own
